bull_bear.body:
- 87-year legacy with strong brand equity and a robust distribution network across India
- Presence in institutional and government supply segments provides a stable revenue base
- Focus on infusion therapy positions the company uniquely within the pharmaceutical landscape
- Flagship company of the diversified Kothari Group
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Material cost / raw material price volatility — Supply chain challenges and elevated raw material or resource costs could adversely impact availability and overall product cost structure, resulting in diminished margins; company mitigates via alternative specifications/sourcing, inventory regulation for bulk discounts and price locking.
- Geopolitical disruption and global supply chain volatility — Geopolitical disruption could impact global supply chains and strain business-as-usual operations; the company is exposed to changes in input prices, international logistics, forex movements and availability of key starting materials, APIs, excipients and packaging materials.
- Climate change (physical and transition risk) — By 2026 the pharmaceutical industry faces intense scrutiny over its carbon footprint; company categorises exposure into Physical Risks and Transition Risks and reviews its product portfolio for resilience against seasonal variability and climate change.
- Increasing competition and pricing pressure — Intense pressure from both large-scale generic leaders (with large R&D budgets and economies of scale) and agile niche competitors; competitors are aggressively slashing prices in the Large Volume Parenterals (LVP) and IV fluid segments, risking irrational price behaviour industry-wide.
- Currency fluctuation exposure — Unprecedented swings in foreign exchange rates driven by global geopolitical crisis may create short-term margin pressure from elevated material costs or depressed revenue realisations; the company is sensitive to the USD/INR exchange rate given its export operations.
- Evolving regulatory / compliance requirements — Regulatory authorities are moving toward a risk-based approach across the pharma industry; drug establishment licenses, safety, health and environmental laws could change, negatively impacting operations, finances and business if compliance lags.
- Single-segment business concentration — The Company operates in a single segment and therefore its performance could not be segregated in terms of business verticals or geographical presence, per Note No. 60 to the financial statements, indicating limited diversification.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Albert David Limited manufactures and trades pharmaceutical formulations, infusion solutions, herbal dosage forms and bulk drugs (APIs), and is the flagship company of the diversified Kothari Group, headquartered in Kolkata with operations across India and overseas. It has a longstanding presence in institutional and government supply segments and is positioned uniquely within the pharmaceutical landscape through its focus on infusion therapy.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Continue building on the company's 87-year legacy, grounded in values of quality, reliability, integrity and responsibility, growing thoughtfully with discipline for long-term stability
- Strengthen manufacturing capabilities, make the supply chain more efficient and keep quality standards robust and consistent
- Build brands by creating a strong prescriber base and developing Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs), further strengthening portfolio and market presence
- Continue focus on quality, compliance and manufacturing excellence, particularly Revised Schedule-M compliance, process improvement and technology-led efficiency
- R&D Centre (DSIR-recognized since 2013) focused on formulation and API development, process optimization, quality enhancement and troubleshooting, with significant emphasis on expanding the product portfolio in Human Placenta Extract-based therapies and exploring synergistic combinations with other therapeutic compounds
- Adopt latest technology and stay in continuous touch with foreign manufacturers/machine suppliers to upgrade units for effective cost control
- Steady/consistent dividend policy: Board proposed a dividend for F.Y. 2025-26 in line with the company's steady dividend policy, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM; no amount was transferred to any reserves during the year under review.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: No new plant, capacity addition, acquisition or JV is disclosed in this bundle. The company completed an upgrade of its manufacturing facility to comply with Revised Schedule-M requirements during F.Y. 2025-26, and continues to place emphasis on quality systems, technology adoption and Revised Schedule-M compliance as an ongoing focus for F.Y. 2026-27. The company also completed the WHO-Geneva PQ audit for SSG during the year, supporting regulatory readiness for export opportunities.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's pharmaceutical industry (valued at over USD $50 billion) continues to grow consistently, strengthening India's position as a trusted global supplier of generic medicines
- Established product portfolio, focus on compliance and initiatives such as the WHO-Geneva PQ audit completion strengthen readiness to respond to export/international opportunities, subject to regulatory approvals, market conditions and customer requirements
- Export opportunities remain linked to global demand conditions, currency movements, logistics costs, regulatory requirements and pricing pressures in overseas markets; a slowdown in major economies or geopolitical disruption may affect export demand visibility, shipment timelines and market access
- Presence in institutional and government supply segments provides a stable revenue base, while focus on infusion therapy positions the company uniquely within the pharmaceutical landscape
- Higher trade barriers, geopolitical disruptions and elevated inflation may increase procurement, freight, energy and compliance-related costs, and affect delivery schedules and working-capital requirements
- Continued manufacturing of SSG injections for Kala Azar, with rare-disease/specialty focus supported by favourable regulatory pathways industry-wide
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

open.item: Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5.00 per equity share of Rs. 10/- each (50%) for F.Y. 2025-26, subject to shareholder approval at the 87th AGM, resulting in a cash outflow of Rs. 285.39 Lakhs.
Board proposed a dividend of Rs. 5.00/- (50%) per equity share of Rs. 10/- each for the financial year ending 31st March, 2026, in line with the company's steady dividend policy.

For F.Y. 2026-27, strategic priorities include expanding market reach, strengthening existing brands, developing selected new product categories and improving engagement with healthcare professionals and institutional customers.
R&D team is working on new molecules to strengthen the new product pipeline and drug delivery systems, including progressing development of Miltefosine, a more advanced molecule for Kala Azar.

R&D Centre placing significant emphasis on expanding the product portfolio in Human Placenta Extract-based therapies and exploring synergistic combinations with other therapeutic compounds; during the year, work advanced on standardization of bio-constituents in placenta-based formulations.
